documents.unit: Division of Information Resources & Technology and Office of the Provost
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy (University Policies)
documents.stance_why: Its core rules are "must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data" into public AI tools and "must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms"; these limit AI to approved settings, so restrict. For coursework it only says AI requirements "must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy" and sets no stance.
documents.summary: A university information-security policy that governs AI use with Rowan data. It bars entering confidential data into public AI tools and limits university business to approved platforms. Coursework rules are passed to the Academic Integrity Policy.

units.why: The stated purpose frames the whole policy as secure use of AI and LLMs with Rowan data, so it is an institution-level framework (P56) rather than a rule for one group.
units.anchor: establish requirements for the secure use of AI and Large Language Models

units.why: "The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies" binds every user to existing university policy, which is P77 (comply with existing policy) and not a new AI-specific rule.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies

units.why: The sentence says all community members "must adhere" to legal, ethical and academic-integrity requirements on data, privacy, ownership and integrity, which is compliance with existing rules (P77); it names academic integrity but sets no integrity rule itself.
units.anchor: must adhere to human resource and legal requirements, as well as ethical standards

units.why: Employees are told AI meeting transcripts "may create records subject to" OPRA; this is a legal-compliance warning (P77), phrased as awareness and not a ban.
units.anchor: AI generated transcripts of meetings may create records subject to OPRA
units.policy: Rowan employees should be aware that AI-generated transcripts of meetings may create records subject to OPRA unless eligible for a specific exemption.

units.why: "must not enter ... confidential, proprietary or regulated data ... into publicly-available AI tools" is a data-protection ban (P50), the nearest type; it forbids a use so it is a restriction.
units.anchor: must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data
units.fit_note: P50 says protect data and prefer vetted tools; this unit is a flat prohibition on entering classified data into public AI tools.

units.why: "must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms" limits all university business, including academic work, to approved tools; P50 (prefer vetted tools) is nearest but this is mandatory, not a preference.
units.anchor: must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms
units.fit_note: Type P50 says "prefer" vetted tools; Rowan makes approved platforms mandatory for university business, including academic communications.

units.why: "must be procured through the standard processes" of IRT and Contracting governs buying AI services, an institutional purchasing control closest to P65 (vendor review).
units.anchor: must be procured through the standard processes
units.policy: Subscriptions and purchases of AI services must be procured through the standard processes of IRT and the Office of Contracting & Procurement.
units.fit_note: P65 is about review of vendor agreements and data sharing; this unit only routes AI purchases through standard procurement.

units.why: Recording of internal meetings by AI "may only" use IRT-authorized platforms; this is an operational AI rule (P76), not about teaching.
units.anchor: may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized, secured and managed by IRT

units.why: AI transcription of confidential HR meetings "should not be used" without prior HR permission; operational use of AI in HR processes, so P76.
units.anchor: AI transcriptions of confidential Human Resources meetings
units.policy: AI transcriptions of confidential HR meetings, including candidate interviews, should not be used unless prior HR permission is obtained and safeguards are implemented.

units.why: "AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy" hands coursework rules to another policy and sets none itself; P77 (comply with existing policy) fits, not P04 since no instructor is named.
units.anchor: AI requirements related to coursework must comply with

units.why: "Questions ... should be directed to" Ethics, Academic Integrity or Research offices points people to human offices for help (P72), the closest type.
units.anchor: Questions regarding the use of AI or data mining tools should be directed
units.fit_note: P72 is about students being pointed to human help; here all community members are pointed to Ethics, Academic Integrity or Research offices.

units.why: "may not infringe on copyright laws" forbids AI use that violates copyright and the University Copyright Policy, which matches P52.
units.anchor: The use of AI may not infringe on copyright laws

units.why: The sentence requires AI use in research, including AI development, to follow governing research policies; that is P62 (AI in research).
units.anchor: AI use in Research, including the development of AI and other machine learning

units.why: Violators "shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal" states penalties for breaking this policy; P37 is nearest but the sanctions target employees and community members, not students.
units.anchor: shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal from the University
units.frag_end: civil and criminal penalties, if applicable.
units.fit_note: P37 concerns penalties for student AI misuse in courses; this states discipline for any person violating the IRT data-security AI policy.

units.why: Exceptions "must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of the Provost" creates an exception process, which no listed type covers.
units.anchor: Any exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office
units.uncovered_note: Exceptions to the AI policy require approval from the Information Security Office and the Provost.

units.why: The Provost, CIO and ISO "shall ensure compliance" while VPs and Deans "shall implement", assigning responsibility for the policy; no listed type covers allocation of accountability for implementing the policy.
units.anchor: shall ensure compliance with this policy. The Vice Presidents and Deans shall implement this policy
units.frag_start: Under the direction of the President
units.uncovered_note: Names which officers ensure compliance with and implement the AI policy.

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence & Teaching
documents.stance_why: The page says "The University does not have a universal generative AI policy. Instructors may select one of the following statements", and offers four sample statements from ban to some-use to generic, so it delegates and lists tiers.
documents.summary: Faculty Center page that says Rowan has no universal GenAI policy and gives instructors four sample syllabus statements. It also advises against relying on AI detectors and on following up with students, and lists many outside resources.

units.why: "The University does not have a universal generative AI policy" says there is no university-wide rule, so the decision lies with instructors (P04); it sets no stance itself.
units.anchor: The University does not have a universal generative AI policy

units.why: The Senate Task Force "recommendation" that faculty put "a clear and specific statement in their syllabi and Canvas" asks instructors to state AI expectations, which is P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a clear and specific statement in their syllabi and Canvas
units.frag_end: may or may not be used in their classes.

units.why: Offering four sample statements from which instructors "may select one" defines named options from no AI to some AI to generic (P05), though the document sets no level itself.
units.anchor: Instructors may select one of the following statements if appropriate

units.why: Option 1 says "any use" of GenAI "will be considered a violation of academic integrity", a blanket ban for the course (P01) offered as sample text.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of academic integrity and will be treated accordingly
units.policy: Sample statement: in this course, any use of generative AI such as ChatGPT, DALL-E, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and others will be considered a violation of academic integrity and will be treated accordingly.

units.why: Option 1 lists that students "may fail the assignment, fail the course, or face other sanctions", concrete penalties (P37).
units.anchor: may fail the assignment, fail the course, or face other sanctions

units.why: "Violations that result in a grade penalty must be reported to the Provost's Office" is a reporting duty in the integrity process; P36 is nearest.
units.anchor: Violations that result in a grade penalty must be reported to the Provost's Office
units.fit_note: P36 classifies AI misuse as misconduct; this unit adds that graded violations must be reported to the Provost's Office.

units.why: "students should provide appropriate documentation whenever quoting, paraphrasing, summarizing, or otherwise using the language or ideas of others" asks for attribution, P24.
units.anchor: students should provide appropriate documentation whenever quoting, paraphrasing, summarizing
units.fit_note: Wording is general plagiarism attribution, not specific to AI.

units.why: Option 2 opens by saying assignments exist "to help you develop key skills" and to assess mastery; it explains why AI is restricted, i.e. P41 (AI shortcuts the practice).
units.anchor: The purpose of the assignments in this course is to help you develop key skills

units.why: Option 2 states that using GenAI "or other unauthorized tools on these assignments defeats the purpose" and is "an academic integrity violation": a ban on AI for these assignments, P01.
units.anchor: Using generative AI or other unauthorized tools on these assignments defeats the purpose

units.why: "misrepresents your mastery of the material" argues that AI hides what a student knows, a false picture of mastery (P43).
units.anchor: misrepresents your mastery of the material
units.fit_note: The text says AI misrepresents mastery to the instructor, not that students fool themselves.

units.why: "please let me know" invites students unsure about allowed resources to ask the instructor, P10.
units.anchor: what resources may be allowed on a specific assignment please let me know

units.why: Option 3 allows GenAI "as a tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)", a permitted use for brainstorming and feedback (P15).
units.anchor: used as a tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)
units.fit_note: Also covers feedback, not only idea generation.

units.why: "work submitted by a student should be that of the student and not the work of an AI system" bars submitting AI-made work as one's own (P19), phrased as "should".
units.anchor: should be that of the student and not the work of an AI system

units.why: "it should be cited like any other reference material" requires citing AI-generated material, P24.
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material

units.why: "the student bears responsibility for any inaccuracies or misinformation" says students own AI errors, matching P31 (verify output) most closely.
units.anchor: the student bears responsibility for any inaccuracies or misinformation
units.fit_note: States responsibility for errors; it does not tell students to verify.

units.why: "please reach out to your instructor" directs unsure students to ask the instructor about AI use under the integrity policy (P10).
units.anchor: please reach out to your instructor
units.frag_start: If you have questions about how

units.why: Option 4 says students "must follow all instructor guidelines on the use or prohibition of generative AI", leaving the rule to the instructor (P04) and binding students to it.
units.anchor: you must follow all instructor guidelines on the use or prohibition of generative AI

units.why: "The unauthorized use of generative AI on assignments may be considered cheating" classifies unauthorized AI as cheating under the integrity policy (P36).
units.anchor: unauthorized use of generative AI on assignments may be considered cheating

units.why: "Submitting the output of generative AI without citation is considered plagiarism" makes nondisclosure the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Submitting the output of generative AI without citation is considered plagiarism

units.why: "you are responsible for any inaccuracies or information within your submitted assignments" makes students answerable for what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: you are responsible for any inaccuracies or information within your submitted assignments

units.why: "Faculty also might choose to list the ways that generative AI could be used" invites instructors to specify allowed uses per assignment (P04).
units.anchor: Faculty also might choose to list the ways that generative AI could be used

units.why: The Task Force links a Syllabi Policies repository so instructors "see the range of policies" before writing their own, which supports faculty in learning about options (P63).
units.anchor: helping other instructors see the range of policies available by other educators
units.frag_start: for the purposes of sharing and
units.fit_note: The page points to a resource of example policies rather than offering training.

units.why: The page offers a "Canvas module designed specifically for Rowan students" with an AI literacy introduction, which is student AI-literacy provision (P70).
units.anchor: Introduction to AI Literacy for Students
units.frag_start: Introduction to AI Literacy for Students

units.why: The page provides "Rowan-licensed GenAI tools and guidelines for using them", pointing to sanctioned university tools (P17).
units.anchor: overview of Rowan-licensed GenAI tools and guidelines for using them

units.why: The Elon guide helps students develop "uniquely human capabilities that allow us to work with, and direct powerful AI technologies", framing AI skill as an asset (P44).
units.anchor: uniquely human capabilities that allow us to work with, and direct powerful AI technologies
units.frag_start: This Rowan approved field guide from

units.why: "we do NOT recommend relying on any of the numerous AI Content Detector programs" tells faculty not to rely on detectors (P39).
units.anchor: we do NOT recommend relying on any of the numerous

units.why: The page says detectors "have not yet demonstrated their accuracy" and produce "false positives", giving the reason for P39.
units.anchor: Such programs have not yet demonstrated their accuracy and do not provide hard evidence

units.why: "results from these detectors will not be considered as evidence for a Rowan Report of an Academic Integrity Violation" bars detector output as proof (P39).
units.anchor: results from these detectors will not be considered as evidence

units.why: "other forms of evidence may be used to make a report" says what can support a misuse finding in place of detectors, which fits P69 only partly.
units.anchor: other forms of evidence may be used to make a report
units.fit_note: Says other evidence may be used but sets no standard of proof or examples.

units.why: The page tells faculty to check "citations and quotations" because AI "may create fictitious citations"; AI error as a risk, closest to P31.
units.anchor: may not cite them correctly or may create fictitious citations
units.fit_note: Addressed to faculty as a way to spot misuse, not to students to verify their output.

units.why: "fabrication is a form of academic dishonesty" classifies invented sources as misconduct that faculty can report (P36).
units.anchor: fabrication is a form of academic dishonesty

units.why: "faculty must file an AIV report if they wish to sanction a student" sets the procedure for sanctions, part of the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: faculty must file an AIV report if they wish to sanction a student
units.fit_note: P36 classifies misuse as misconduct; this adds that only a filed AIV report can lead to a sanction.

units.why: "Schedule a time to discuss the topic of the paper with the student" tells faculty to talk with the student before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: Schedule a time to discuss the topic of the paper with the student

units.why: "initiate the discussion in a nonconfrontational manner" asks for a respectful tone in the follow-up, part of P57.
units.anchor: initiate the discussion in a nonconfrontational manner

units.why: Building the follow-up "into the course structure so students are not singled out" is a course design idea for checking understanding (P34).
units.anchor: built into the course structure so students are not singled out
units.fit_note: Suggests building routine follow-up conversations into the course.

units.why: The "AI-Resistant Pedagogy Studio" toolkit for "Assignment Redesign" is recommended to faculty to learn about redesign; a resource for faculty learning, P63.
units.anchor: An Interactive Toolkit for Assignment Redesign

documents.title: GenAI at Rowan: For Students
documents.stance_why: It says "Using GenAI in a course without the permission of the instructor may lead to an academic integrity violation" and to "follow the guidelines given by your instructor", so the decision sits with the course instructor and the guide sets no stance of its own.
documents.summary: Library guide for students that lists Rowan-approved GenAI tools and says use needs instructor permission. It warns that AI output can be false and points to citation guides.

units.why: "Using GenAI in a course without the permission of the instructor may lead to an academic integrity violation" sets a default of no AI unless the instructor permits, a fallback (P06).
units.anchor: without the permission of the instructor may lead to an academic integrity violation
units.policy: Using GenAI in a course without the permission of the instructor may lead to an academic integrity violation and have serious sanctions attached.

units.why: "check the syllabus or clarify with your instructor" tells students to confirm what is allowed, P10.
units.anchor: check the syllabus or clarify with your instructor whether they allow

units.why: "follow the guidelines given by your instructor for a specific course" leaves rules to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: it is important to follow the guidelines given by your instructor for a specific course
units.frag_start: As with any resource or tool,

units.why: "approved by Rowan in terms of data protection" explains that the listed tools are vetted for data, P50.
units.anchor: The tools below are approved by Rowan in terms of data protection

units.why: "GenAI tools may confidently state false information, make up facts, quotations and citations" warns that AI output is unreliable, P31.
units.anchor: GenAI tools may confidently state false information, make up facts, quotations and citations

units.why: "be sure to engage carefully and thoughtfully with the generated content" asks students to evaluate output critically, P31.
units.anchor: be sure to engage carefully and thoughtfully with the generated content

units.why: Copilot is "available for students through their Rowan email address with commercial data protection": a university-provided AI tool, P17.
units.anchor: available for students through their Rowan email address with

units.why: "Student data is not used to train the underlying language models" is a data-privacy assurance about the approved tool, P50.
units.anchor: Student data is not used to train the underlying language models

units.why: Gemini is "available for students who are registered in the current term" with "enterprise-grade data protection": another provided tool, P17.
units.anchor: available for students who are registered in the current term or a future term

units.why: "there is currently no way to delete Gemini chats in Workspace accounts" is a data-retention caution about a tool, P50.
units.anchor: there is currently no way to delete Gemini chats in Workspace accounts

units.why: Firefly is "available for students who are enrolled in some College of Communication & Creative Arts courses", a limited-access provided tool, P17.
units.anchor: available for students who are enrolled in some College of Communication & Creative Arts courses

units.why: The guide links citation formats for ChatGPT and other AI generators from APA and MLA, supporting AI citation (P24).
units.anchor: How to cite ChatGPT

units.why: The recommended Student Guide has "7 principles to help with learning about GenAI as well as appropriate use", AI-literacy provision for students, P70.
units.anchor: 7 principles to help with learning about GenAI as well as appropriate use

notes: Rowan has no university-wide academic AI policy (Faculty Center says so); the ISO:2024:01 policy is a data-security policy. No school or computing unit policy found. Course layer deferred.
